I can’t run continuous background monitoring or “ping” you later unless you set up a real automation I can trigger or you run a script/service yourself. I can, however, help in three practical ways — pick one and I’ll proceed:

1) I check it right now
- If you can paste the URL where the PDF will appear (or upload the PDF once it’s available), I’ll inspect the file immediately and produce the rundown of the Risk Factors section.

2) I give you a ready-to-run monitor that notifies you when the PDF appears
- Below is a concise Python script you can run on a server/VM or as a scheduled job (cron, systemd, GitHub Actions, or AWS Lambda). It polls a URL until the PDF is available, downloads it, extracts the "Risk Factors" text and sends a notification via Slack webhook or email. You can run it locally or deploy to a small cloud instance.

Python monitor (outline + code)
- Requirements: Python 3.8+, pip install requests PyPDF2 slack-sdk (or use requests to post webhook).
- Set environment variables: MONITOR_URL, POLL_SECONDS (e.g., 60), SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL or SMTP settings (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, NOTIFY_EMAIL).

Code (save as monitor_pdf.py):
```
import os, time, io, requests, smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage
from PyPDF2 import PdfReader

URL = os.environ.get("MONITOR_URL")
POLL_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("POLL_SECONDS","60"))
SLACK_WEBHOOK = os.environ.get("SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL")
NOTIFY_EMAIL = os.environ.get("NOTIFY_EMAIL")

def download_pdf(url):
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=20)
    if r.status_code == 200 and r.headers.get("content-type","").lower().startswith("application/pdf"):
        return io.BytesIO(r.content)
    return None

def extract_risk_factors(pdf_bytes, chars=2000):
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_bytes)
    full = []
    for p in reader.pages:
        try:
            full.append(p.extract_text() or "")
        except:
            full.append("")
    text = "\n".join(full)
    idx = text.lower().find("risk factors")
    if idx == -1:
        return None
    snippet = text[idx: idx + chars]
    # Try to cut at next major heading (simple heuristics)
    for sep in ["\n\n", "\nItem", "\nForward-looking", "\nSpecial Note"]:
        pos = snippet.find(sep, 20)
        if pos>0:
            snippet = snippet[:pos]
            break
    return snippet.strip()

def notify_slack(webhook, message):
    if not webhook: return
    payload = {"text": message}
    requests.post(webhook, json=payload, timeout=10)

def notify_email(to_addr, subject, body):
    host = os.environ.get("SMTP_HOST")
    port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT","587"))
    user = os.environ.get("SMTP_USER")
    passwd = os.environ.get("SMTP_PASS")
    if not host or not to_addr:
        return
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = user
    msg["To"] = to_addr
    msg["Subject"] = subject
    msg.set_content(body)
    with smtplib.SMTP(host, port) as s:
        s.starttls()
        s.login(user, passwd)
        s.send_message(msg)

def main():
    print("Monitoring", URL)
    while True:
        try:
            pdf = download_pdf(URL)
            if pdf:
                rf = extract_risk_factors(pdf)
                summary = rf or "(Risk Factors heading not found - full text attached or review recommended)"
                message = f"PDF detected at {URL}\n\nRisk Factors (approx):\n{summary}"
                notify_slack(SLACK_WEBHOOK, message)
                if NOTIFY_EMAIL:
                    notify_email(NOTIFY_EMAIL, "Quarterly filing PDF available — Risk Factors", message)
                print("Notified. Exiting monitor.")
                return
        except Exception as e:
            print("Error:", e)
        time.sleep(POLL_SECONDS)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Notes/limitations:
- PDF parsing can be imperfect (headings, two-column layouts, scanned PDFs). The extraction above is heuristic — it looks for the text "Risk Factors" and pulls a chunk. You may want to use more advanced PDF tools (pdfminer.six, Tika, or OCR for scanned PDFs) if accuracy is critical.
- Polling frequency: don’t set too aggressive a poll interval against public sites (respect rate limits).
- Delivery: Slack webhooks are easiest. Email requires SMTP credentials. I can also show how to push to SMS via Twilio or to Microsoft Teams.

3) I prepare a notification/rundown template you’ll receive
- Example template I’ll send when the PDF is detected:
  - File + timestamp
  - Short summary (3–5 bullets) of top risk factors
  - Severity/impact score (low/medium/high) per factor with short rationale
  - Actions to consider (e.g., further analysis, legal review, investor comms)
  - Link to full Risk Factors text and page references (if extractable)
